observations: The direct current failure is real_tool.case_board_interface_discovery: the progressive/final selector evidence is inconsistent, wrapper_top_module is missing, selected_cell_id is not a Vivado cell fact, timing and AXI contracts are unresolved, and the selected slot does not expose the required 512-bit AXI data.
The current CCTG closure classifies this as a verification-capability gap, not a localized RTL defect. No current failed boundary, root candidate module, or executed board trace is available.

The prior repair execution is incomplete and blocked. Its VCS Error-[ITSFM] Illegal `timescale for module` report lacks the offending absolute pathname, line/context, exact command and ordered source list, language modes, effective options, and editable-versus-read-only source provenance. The historical diagnosis is therefore not executable repair evidence.

The operator-leaf and single-transformer-layer certificates are live and reusable. Hierarchical learning context requires preserving their elastic variable-latency token-pipeline semantics and reopening them only for a current trace that directly contradicts a named invariant; no such contradiction is present.

The board simulation and all downstream board gates are dependency-skipped or not_run. There is consequently no board-level value, numeric, order, AXI, DDR, liveness, weight-consumption, or output-frontier claim. Independent AXI or prefetch progress, if later observed, must not be treated as output-frontier progress.

Board semantic evidence is missing. Any retry must use the same immutable checkpoint and stimulus, an independent target-model inference for that checkpoint/input, the frozen numeric policy and tolerance, generated semantic testbench hashes, complete required-scope tensor hashes, and proof that every Transformer-block weight was consumed by the DUT.

sacg_memory_truth reports 16 active contamination barriers and six open retry requests in this scope; rejected Stage7 and Stage8 artifacts remain debug evidence only until a refined contract passes. The scope has no open backtrack request, so no lower-layer backtrack is authorized.
The conditional specialist review was no_split and supplies no substitute evidence or repair decision.
proposed_actions: Obtain a bounded, fact-bound board-interface discovery reconciliation from the exact sample project and real Vivado exports; request approval rather than guessing if wrapper or compute target remains ambiguous.
Capture complete VCS compiler diagnostic and source-identity provenance before any board-source modification.
After both contracts pass, rerun the current board layer through the Stage7 dependency DAG with immutable semantic and board-wrapper inputs.

If the executed board simulation then fails, generate a current hash-bound boundary trace and causal slice before proposing any code repair; preserve lower certificates unless the trace explicitly contradicts them.
Apply only a localized board wrapper, runtime, or verification-harness repair after causal localization, then rerun the same board layer until all required gates pass.
risks: Guessing wrapper_top_module, compute-cell identity, AXI width, compile executable, or source ordering would violate the human-boundary and exact-board-source constraints.
Editing board or certified-kernel sources before VCS provenance is captured could be speculative and causally unassignable.
Running downstream simulation or semantic assemblers before board-interface identity and compile-plan binding are repaired would produce dependency-skipped evidence rather than acceptance evidence.
Changing checkpoint, stimulus, target-model reference, numeric tolerance, testbench contract, or wrapper hashes during repair would contaminate the comparison.
A board output-frontier stall alone cannot identify a lower-layer RTL root cause; a lower-layer replay requires direct current ingress/start/egress and named causal-boundary contradiction evidence.
Repeated repair of the same class without fresh intervention-response evidence may cause repair-loop spinning.
